title: Automated Robotic Dispensing Technique for Surface Guidance and Bioprinting of Cells
protocol: Use polystyrene sheets for surface modification since tissue culture plates tend to bow upwards in the center.
Select a pressure of 2 bar on the regulator of the oxygen cylinder connected to the plasma machine.
Switch the plasma machine on and input conditions: 150 W, 30 sscm of oxygen, 10 min (for power, gas flow, and time respectively).
Place polystyrene substrate into the plasma chamber, seal the door, and press start button on control panel.
Soak oxygen plasma treated polystyrene substrate in fetal bovine serum and incubate at 37 °C for 2 hr.
Wash three times with 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Program to etch surface using a stylus or scalpel.
Insert a 1.5 mm diameter textile needle into the nozzle of a dispensing syringe until it is wedged and secured.
Choose a round handled scalpel for fastening into the clamp mechanism of the printing arm.
Sketch the desired pattern on graph paper with numbered axes to generate X-Y coordinates.
Input the coordinates of the etched/bioprinted pattern into spreadsheet software.
Open the print/dispensing software.
Select "Program > Add Program" followed by "Edit > Add Point" to set up the program.
Export x and y coordinate values from the spreadsheet into the print/dispensing software using the "Copy and Paste" function.
Calibrate the z height of the robot before each run.
Select the "Robot" option in the print/dispensing software.
Click on "Changing Mode" and enable the "Teaching mode" option.
Initialize the robot to its default position by selecting "Robot > Meca Initialize".
Select "Robot > Jog" from the menu bar.
Input numerical values (in mm) in the "X and Y slots" to place the stylus exactly on the origin of the pattern.
Input a numerical value (in mm) in the "Z slot" to place the stylus or printing nozzle in contact with the surface but not flex or indent it.
Designate this point as the "Z" starting value.
Select the print instruction for each coordinate point, such as "Start of Line Dispense" to define the first point and print initiation.
Designate intermediate points using "Line Passing".
Signal the robot to terminate the print run with "End of Line Dispense".
Communicate the program to the robot by selecting "Robot > Send C&T Data".
Change the robot to "Run mode" by selecting "Robot > Changing Mode > Switch Run Mode".
Press the green "start button" on the robot dispenser console.
Dissolve 2% gelatin in Minimum Essential Medium Alpha Medium (αMEM) supplemented with 10% FBS and 2% antibiotic/antimycotic at 60 °C for 2 hr to prepare the bioink solutions.
Pre-culture Red Fluorescent Protein expressing Mesenchymal Stem Cells (RFP-MSCs) to 70% confluence in 10 cm tissue culture dishes using αMEM/10% FBS.
Remove the medium and coat RFP-MSCs with 1x trypsin-EDTA solution for 5 min at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,000 x g for 5 min and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 0.5 ml of 1x PBS and count the cell density using a hemocytometer.
Gently mix sufficient volume of RFP-MSCs suspension to achieve a final concentration of 5 x 10^6 cells/ml in the cooled bioink solution.
Pour the cell bearing bioink into a printing syringe with the nozzle sealed.
Chill the loaded syringe to 4 °C to attain printable viscosity.
Place the loaded syringe on the automated robotic dispensing system and attach the air pressure lines.
Remove the syringe Luer seal and attach the print nozzle.
Extrude cellularized bioinks into thin lines using 0.05 MPa back pressure.
Write the bioinks at a speed of 5 mm/sec from a 10 ml syringe via a 27 G needle/nozzle onto a polystyrene film surface.
Follow the pre-programmed deposition pattern to place the cellularized bioink onto pre-etched grooves.
Incubate the extruded lines at room temperature for 1 hour.
Add 10 ml of growth media supplemented with 10% FBS and antibiotics.
Incubate the cells for 24 hours to allow them to sense and react to the etched features.
View the cells using an inverted fluorescence microscope at 10X magnification.
